> While Debian does have split packages for many of the libraries;
> I would like to note that the source packages for the cases mentioned do not share the lib${pkgname} naming scheme

You are confusing source packages with binary packages. Our repo is for binary packages, not source packages. sqlite is the upstream source project name hence also used as source package name by debian. During binary package creation, it is split into libsqlite for libraries and sqlite for binaries. If you depend a package on a combined package containing both libs and binaries, but package only requires libraries, then binaries will needlessly be installed, increasing download and install size for user, and wouldn't be clear if package depends on libs, binaries, or both, like licy said.

> A Debian source package contains the source material used to construct one or more binary packages.

- https://www.debian.org/doc/debian-policy/ch-source.html
- https://www.debian.org/doc/debian-policy/ch-binary.html

payload.author: agnostic-apollo
payload.body: If you are concerned that sqlite should be the source "directory" name, then rename libsqlite directory to sqlite, make current sqlite.subpackage as main package, and create a libsqlite.subpackage, as truboxl suggested. But that issue exists with other packages too.

and yes, so there are two ways that `bash` can be set into login shell mode:

- one is by the `-l` argument to `bash`,
- and another is by setting the `argv[0][0]` character of `bash`'s initial `argv` to `-` before launching it


Termux's `login` command sets `bash` to login shell mode when the `TERM` environment variable is externally set, which conveniently lines up with `agetty` doing that without me having to force anything there, using the `-l` argument method:

https://github.com/termux/termux-tools/blob/9463f66b650383a896fb728579f0dd54bc9ebe5b/scripts/login.in#L82

and normal desktop linux's `login` command implementation sets `bash` to login shell mode seemingly only conditionally on whether a `login` argument for the shell `argv[0]` was manually set to something else, by using the `argv[0][0]` replacing method:

https://github.com/shadow-maint/shadow/blob/33c1736e03be2cefbc1143ffaec896d7139d3cae/lib/shell.c#L51

payload.author: robertkirkman
payload.body:
>  Are you happy with the current versions of `etc/profile` and `etc/bash.bashrc`?

Yes, in this PR I think I am, but what I'm not sure about is whether agnostic-apollo would be. I haven't personally touched the issue or PR involving `~/.bashrc` being sourced by `etc/profile`, even though that doesn't happen in desktop linux, because of the large amount of other changes that agnostic-apollo historically requested.

Very notably, the biggest user impact of this change would be that **the default Termux App terminal starting shell, from the Termux App APK (and also the codepath from `ssh` clients connecting to Termux as well), would not automatically source `~/.bashrc` anymore without users adding the quick setup of that manually, because of the Termux App APK starting shell being a login shell**.

Workarounds for people whose workflow that breaks are going to be, best to start talking about them sooner rather than later for visibility if we are really going to do this:

1. (easy) type `bash` at the starting terminal to get a nested shell that will be a non-login shell, which will automatically source the preexisting `~/.bashrc` if the user had one
2. (harder) manually type this content into **`~/.bash_profile`** and save it:

```bash
if [ -f ~/.bashrc ]; then
  . ~/.bashrc
fi
```

The behavior would, indeed, bring Termux slightly closer to desktop linux, and desktop linux users have already had to learn that they need to manually save that in `.bash_profile` in order to use `~/.bashrc` in login shells, but Termux users definitely have not been used to that. It is, though, necessary with no way around it, i guess, if this is a priority to fix:

- https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/issues/25264

payload.author: robertkirkman
payload.body:
@fornwall you intentionally designed Termux in such a way that you deliberately added sourcing `~/.bashrc` from login shells, stated explicitly in the commit messages, and left it this way for 10 years,

https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/commit/b428c1fca506c1b516cb3c8abc8ab80c456336d7

https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/commit/f4eefdf906c8cbc92b4db449411e1fa7db53b306

reflecting on this, now Tomjo2000, Rudxain, nero and various other users have been complaining about this over the years and are attempting to change Termux to not do that and instead require sourcing `~/.bashrc` manually in login shells from `~/.bash_profile`, just like desktop linux.

would you strongly prefer that Termux remain this way and not remove the sourcing that you placed there, since it might be the best workaround for sourcing `~/.bashrc` from login shells that Termux has, or are you open to changes like this?

nero mentioned the `/etc/skel` mechanism, which many distros do use including Debian and Gentoo, and currently Termux doesn't _really_ have that, BUT,

@TomJo2000 the closest thing Termux _does_ have to an `/etc/skel` mechanism is **this**, the `etc/profile.d/init-termux-properties.sh`, of `termux-tools`,

https://github.com/termux/termux-tools/blob/9463f66b650383a896fb728579f0dd54bc9ebe5b/init-termux-properties.sh.in#L3


which **does** create the file `~/.termux/termux.properties` if it doesn't already exist **directly** in the new Termux `$HOME` folder, which I think very few other packages in Termux do.


Do you think there might be any benefit, or a reliable way to create the needed `~/.bash_profile` that way if one doesn't already exist, using an `etc/profile.d/` file, or do you think that's likely to just result in a race condition or chicken-and-egg problem for the first login?

payload.author: robertkirkman
payload.body: In this message, agnostic-apollo was also originally talking about Debian's `/etc/skel` and `termux-tools`' `etc/profile.d/init-termux-properties.sh`, before anyone else, but as far as I can tell, nobody before me has mentioned concern over whether a chicken-and-egg problem or race condition might occur due to the `bash` command itself needing to create its own `.bash_profile`, as opposed to `adduser`'s `/etc/skel` mechanism on desktop linux running long before `bash` is started as the new user. if we try to implement that, we might need to investigate and test that carefully.

payload.author: robertkirkman
payload.body:
Most of the time if someone is clean installing Termux, they're not going to have either a `.bash_profile` _or_ a preexisting `.bashrc`, so we could just ignore older installations and operate assuming that all `.bashrc`s are going to be newly created, and in that case there wouldn't be a chicken-and-egg problem,

but what I'm thinking about is specifically _the first login after someone who already has a `.bashrc` file, but not a `.bash_profile` file, upgrades their termux past this `bash` update_. I think that might leave a window where the session during which the `~/.bash_profile` file is created might not have its `~/.bashrc` sourced, even though it would have been in all sessions before, and would be in all sessions after that.

For users who have no idea what is going on, a sudden bug that goes away as quickly as it came like that might be maddening.

If testing indicates there is no chance of that and `~/.bash_profile` is reliably sourced after being fully created, then that would mean there is no issue here.

payload.author: robertkirkman

Yes, pretty much, though the way you're counting in your chart whether a non-login shell "loads" `etc/profile` differs from how Arch Linux Wiki's chart counts it:

https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Bash#Configuration_files

they mark non-login shells as "no" for `etc/profile` because they don't technically _source_ `etc/profile` themselves, but they do tend to _inherit_ the variables that were set by `etc/profile` from the login shell from which the non-login shell was started. If that's what your chart is implying, then that would make sense.

> So the current PR behavior is inconsistent by that line of reasoning since it sources bash.bashrc but not ~/.bashrc in interactive login shells.

right, but I'm wondering whether we might be able to set that up the way some people think it should be, by auto-creating a `~/.bash_profile` file if one doesn't exist already.

payload.author: robertkirkman
payload.body: Also, on a similar theme of the charts plotting slightly different data, Arch Linux's chart marks `/etc/bash.bashrc` as not technically being sourced directly from login shells, but it does mention that `etc/profile` normally is supposed to source `etc/bash.bashrc` from there, and in turn `etc/profile` is sourced by login shells, so if your chart is implying that, that would make sense.

if it still requires pyside6, and it is too difficult to compile it without pyside6 , then it might be necessary to move it to tur-on-device, but ideally hopefully a way to cross-compile pyside6 can be found. I don't know how.

payload.author: TomJo2000
payload.body:
This is gonna need more testing.
It appears that neither setting `--enable-site-fndir=no`
https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/blob/00cdd178f3ad3edc60bed93f612a69cf6a097f6b/packages/zsh/build.sh#L17
nor the previous hunk in `configure.ac.patch`,
https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/blob/f2a1bd1ae42fbd775c72aa8d58df41b309ba9213/packages/zsh/configure.ac.patch#L1-L13
actually worked to disable the version specific site directory at `$TERMUX_PREFIX/usr/share/zsh/$ZSH_VERSION/functions`.

What we want is a structure similar to what's present in e.g. Arch Linux.
```console
/usr/share/zsh//
├── 5.9/
│   └── help/
├── functions/
├── scripts/
└── site-functions/
```
With only the `help` entries for the built-in commands under a version specific directory.
Whereas we currently have:
```console
data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/
└── 5.9.1/
    ├── functions/
    ├── help/
    └── scripts/
```
(This is also the case for 5.9, at least as far back as 5.9-7, I need to do some earlier builds to confirm.)

payload.author: TomJo2000
payload.body:
Okay, what was missing here was;
```shell
--enable-function-subdirs
--enable-fndir=$TERMUX_PREFIX/share/zsh/functions
--enable-scriptdir=$TERMUX_PREFIX/share/zsh/scripts
```
That way `functions/` and `scripts/` doesn't end up in the versioned directory, only the `help/` directory does.

The `site-functions/` directory is intended to be used for additional vendored completions, similar to e.g. `fish/vendor_completions.d/`.

payload.author: TomJo2000
payload.body:
`--enable-function-subdirs` actually preserves the upstream distinctions between completions categories
The `${fpath[@]}` prior to enabling it is:
```console
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/5.9/functions
```
After enabling it (with newlines inserted between entries for separation)
```console
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/site-functions
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Calendar
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Chpwd
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/AIX
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/Base
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/BSD
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/Cygwin
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/Darwin
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/Debian
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/Linux
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/Mandriva
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/openSUSE
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/Redhat
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/Solaris
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/Unix
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/X
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Completion/Zsh
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Exceptions
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Math
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/MIME
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Misc
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Newuser
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Prompts
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/VCS_Info
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/VCS_Info/Backends
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions/Zle
```
I don't know if keeping that distinction is all that useful.
(Although it wouldn't hurt anything to keep it, just adds extra array entries in a built-in array.)
When I remove `--enable-function-subdirs` from the build the standard `${fpath[@]}` becomes
```console
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/site-functions
/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/share/zsh/functions
```
Which still covers the `site-functions/` by default, which is what we wanted.

I don't have a preference here one way or the other.
But we are not currently splitting these into separate directories.
We are also not currently shipping `site-functions/` in the default `${fpath[@]}` either though,
so if we're making sure that ends up in there we can make sure the functions are differentiated while we're at it.
